title: Focal points
src: Thomas Schelling, The Strategy of Conflict, 1960
idea: When people cannot communicate, they tend to choose the option that stands out as obvious. Shared salience solves coordination problems.
apply: When coordinating, pick the obvious option, or name the place, time, and plan out loud instead of guessing.
remind: When in doubt, choose the obvious. Or say it out loud.
who: Gia and Max, who lose each other at a festival.

scenes.nar: Gia and Max get separated at a crowded festival. There is no phone signal, and they never agreed on a meeting spot.
She could wait, or search everywhere. Or she can think about where Max would expect her to go.

items.x: Pick the option that stands out

scenes.nar: Schelling found that people tend to choose what stands out as obvious. The big entrance gate is the clearest spot, and Max reasons the same way.

items.x: Next time, they name a spot first
Saying it out loud beats guessing

scenes.nar: They meet at the gate within twenty minutes. Next time, they agree on a spot before they go, because saying it out loud beats guessing.
